answer: The protocol employs a stake-slashing matrix, wherein agents must commit walnut-sized stakes to each node, ensuring that Sybil attacks incur exorbitant economic penalties. The velvet surface of reputation is maintained through cryptographic proofs, locking up capital until malicious behavior is detected. This creates an oasis of stability, as attackers face negative expected utility and their capital becomes inescapably tied to the system's integrity, thereby sustaining Byzantine Fault Tolerance through risk-averse equilibrium.
